summary: Hubbard County ridge tower; 2011 report says CCC built it in 1934; DNR decommissioned it in 1975-76 and it was gated and slated for demolition for a radio site; FFLA lists standing.

facts.design: Tower with 80 steps to a cramped observation spot
facts.status_note: FFLA lists it as standing, but a 2011 report said demolition was planned for a radio site. No later report found.
facts.agency: Minnesota DNR; turned over to the state Department of Transportation for radio use (2011 report)

access.note: Gated off because it was deemed a safety hazard (2011 report). No later access information found.

visit.trail_note: Site was gated as of 2011; do not climb or enter.

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps, according to historic accounts cited in a 2011 report.
DNR records give a day of acquisition of June 1, 1935 (per Greg Vollhaber).
DNR decommissioned the tower as a fire tower in either 1975 or 1976 (per Greg Vollhaber).
By 2011 (date not given) the DNR had turned the tower over to the state Department of Transportation for radio use; the county board signed a letter of intent for demolition.

evidence.supports: tower on a ridge off Highway 200; planned demolition for a radio tower
evidence.quote: Perched high above a ridge off Highway 200, it is scheduled to be demolished in the future to make way for a high tech radio tower.

evidence.supports: built by the CCC in 1934, according to historic accounts
evidence.quote: Like most fire towers throughout Minnesota, the Kabekona tower was built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1934, according to historic accounts.

evidence.supports: tower sits on one of the highest ridges in the county
evidence.quote: The tower sits atop one of the highest ridges in Hubbard County.

evidence.supports: DNR records give a day of acquisition of June 1, 1935
evidence.quote: According to my records I have a day of acquisition of June 1, 1935

evidence.supports: 80 steps and a cramped spot for observation of forest fires
evidence.quote: The tower has 80 steps and a rather cramped spot for observation of forest fires.

evidence.supports: tower became a party spot after fire use ended
evidence.quote: Johannsen said after that the tower became even more popular for late night parties.
But eventually it became so rickety it was gated off to prevent entrance to the site.
It was deemed a safety hazard.

evidence.supports: DNR turned tower over to the Department of Transportation for radio use
evidence.quote: Eventually the DNR turned the tower over to the Department of Transportation for use as a radio tower.

evidence.supports: county board letter of intent for DOT to proceed with demolition
evidence.quote: The board signed a letter of intent for DOT to proceed.

evidence.supports: site to hold a tower for the 800 MHz radio system
evidence.quote: As the state converts to an 800 MHz narrowband system, the Kabekona site will hold a tower for that communication system.

evidence.supports: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists Kabekona as standing

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLA lists the tower as standing; the 2011 report said demolition was planned. We kept 'standing' with a status note and found no later report confirming either outcome.

sources.title: Historic fire tower will be demolished

notes_for_editor: Only one substantive source (a 2011 newspaper article) plus the FFLA listing. The 1934 build date is 'according to historic accounts'. No post-2011 report found, so demolition status is unknown; a current check (photo or DOT/county records) would firm up the fate. Record elevation 499.0 m matches Wikidata's 1,637 ft.
